title: Kashmir
hook: a woman has longed for a man she's only heard described; he stands in front of her, and nothing happens, until someone says, that's him

segments.voice: Yesterday in Kashmir, Abhinavagupta and rasa: the taste of a play, and the wide awareness doing the tasting. What moved you, and who noticed? Day one thousand three hundred ninety-one.

A young woman has fallen in love with a man she's never met. She's only heard about him: how kind he is, how he speaks, what he's done. She thinks about him all the time. Then one day he comes to her house. He stands right in front of her. And she feels nothing much; he's just a visitor. Until someone at her side leans over and says: that's him. And everything changes, though not one thing in the room has moved. A teacher in Kashmir used that story to explain what he meant by recognition.
screen: `IN LOVE WITH SOMEONE UNMET.` → `HE STANDS IN FRONT OF HER.` → `THAT'S HIM.`

segments.voice: The teacher is Utpaladeva, a Shaiva thinker of Kashmir, and the story comes, in paraphrase, from his work on recognition. That word is the key: pratyabhijna, recognition. Not finding something new. Recognizing what's already in front of you. Here's how the story fits. In his teaching, Shiva isn't far off. Shiva is the very awareness you're living in, the one who sees and knows, right now. So the problem was never that God is missing. It's like the woman in the story. Her beloved is standing in the room, and she's still longing, because she hasn't recognized him. Nothing needs to be brought in. Something needs to be seen. Second, look at what makes the difference: someone at her side who says, that's him. In Utpaladeva's tradition, that's the role of a teacher and of teaching. The teacher doesn't hand you a new self. The teacher points. Third, notice the joy. She doesn't receive a lecture on who he is. The recognition itself is the delight. And Utpaladeva wasn't only a careful thinker. He also wrote hymns to Shiva, full of longing and tenderness, and the two belong together: the more you see that he's here, the more there is to sing about. And look how the week's Kashmir has been building. A valley drained so a hidden thing could be seen. A history told without bending. A theater where the small self steps aside. Now a woman who simply recognizes who's in the room. Different poets and thinkers, one valley, and a long habit of looking again at what's already here.
screen: `PRATYABHIJNA: RECOGNITION` · `THE BELOVED ALREADY IN THE ROOM` · `THE TEACHER POINTS: THAT'S HIM` · `RECOGNITION IS THE DELIGHT`

segments.voice: Sit, and let the breath slow. Look around the room for a moment, then let your eyes rest or close. Notice that you're aware: of sounds, of the breath, of the body sitting. Don't hunt for anything new. Just notice that this awareness is already here, and has been all day. Whenever the mind goes looking somewhere else, come back and say quietly inside: already here. If you pray, you can turn to God as already present, in your own way. The bell holds the time.
Kashmir. The valley where Utpaladeva taught recognition: the beloved is already in the room, and the teacher simply points. Today's word.
Your line: Kashmir. Today, look again at one familiar person or place as if someone beside you had just said, that's it. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-one.

howItsDone: Students of Kashmir Shaivism study Utpaladeva's teaching on recognition with a teacher, and his hymns to Shiva are read and recited as devotion.
